poster.hook: Halfling, loud, mid-verse. Last seen leaving the Gull & Anchor owing for three pints.

story.appearance: Round, windburned, and ginger, with salt-stiff curls and a patched velvet coat in three clashing shades of blue. Carries a battered lute called Biddy that has a gull-shaped dent in the back.
story.concept: Odo came to Saltmere for one night's work twenty-odd years ago and never left. He wrote the storm-hymn the whole town sings when the bell rings, and he has been dining on it ever since. He is loud, generous, perpetually broke, and the first to laugh at his own jokes, which is how nobody notices he's frightened.
story.stake: Every storm night the town sings his hymn in the dark. If the bell stays silent tonight, the last thing the drowned will hear is a chorus of his words.
story.goal: Get the bell rung with the whole town singing under it, and finally write the last verse.
story.secret: He didn't write the hymn. Twenty years ago he rowed out drunk on a black night and heard it sung from under the water; he scribbled down what he could and called it his own. The final verse never stayed in his head, and every time he tries to play it Biddy's strings go slack and the nearest cup of water starts to shiver. He suspects it's the verse meant for the bell.
story.voice: Warm, theatrical, incorrigible. Calls everyone 'my friend' and narrates tense moments like a minstrel at a feast. Goes quiet and plain-spoken only when he's truly scared.
mannerisms: Tunes Biddy whenever he's about to lie
Hums the hymn's last note, then stops dead
Bows to anything that is about to hit him
story.trinket: A tarnished silver tuning fork that only ever hums the hymn's last note

ties.text: Has sung under her tower every storm night for nineteen years. She calls him 'child' and tells him to hush; she has never once told him to leave.
ties.public: Sings under her bell-tower every storm night

ties.text: She hums a tune he swears he has never played for anyone. It is the last verse.
Rook has picked his pocket twice and given it back once, with interest. Odo considers this a friendship.
ties.public: Rook picks his pocket; Odo calls it friendship

story.intro: "Odo Brambletoe, bard, baritone, and yes, that is my hymn you hear every storm night. No, I don't take requests during a crisis. Well. Perhaps one."

features.name: Brave
features.text: You have Advantage on saving throws against the Frightened condition.

features.name: Halfling Nimbleness
features.text: You can move through the space of any creature that is larger than you, though you can't stop there.

features.name: Luck
features.text: When you roll a 1 on the d20 of a D20 Test, you can reroll the die and must use the new roll.

features.name: Naturally Stealthy
features.text: You can take the Hide action even when you are obscured only by a creature at least one size larger than you.

features.name: Musician: Encouraging Song
features.text: When you finish a Short or Long Rest, play a song on an instrument you know; up to 3 allies who hear it gain Heroic Inspiration.

features.name: Bardic Inspiration (d8)
features.text: Bonus Action: give a creature within 60 ft other than you a d8. Within the next hour, after it fails a D20 Test, it can add the die. You regain all uses on a Short or Long Rest.

features.name: Expertise
features.text: Your proficiency bonus is doubled for Performance and Persuasion.

features.name: Jack of All Trades
features.text: Add half your proficiency bonus (rounded down) to ability checks that don't already include it, Initiative included.

features.name: Font of Inspiration
features.text: Your Bardic Inspiration returns on a Short Rest as well as a Long Rest, and you can spend a spell slot to regain one use.

features.name: Bonus Proficiencies
features.text: You gained three extra skill proficiencies (History, Religion, Deception).

features.name: Cutting Words
features.text: Reaction: spend a Bardic Inspiration die to subtract it from the damage roll, attack roll, or ability check of a creature you can see within 60 ft.

attacks.name: Vicious Mockery
attacks.note: Target has Disadvantage on its next attack roll before the end of its next turn

spellcasting.note: Knows 3 cantrips; prepares 9 bard spells and can swap one after a Long Rest. Uses his lute as a spellcasting focus.

attack.name: Starry Wisp
attack.note: Target sheds dim light until the end of your next turn and can't benefit from being Invisible
